svg.title: Intent to Basket, a quick commerce shopping experiment. Headline: Say the meal. Get the basket. Instead of searching for what you need, tell the store what you want to achieve. Type I want to make biryani for 2 or dinner for 4 under 600 rupees, and the app plans the meal, scales the ingredients to the head count, maps every ingredient to a real catalogue product, works out how many packs to buy, fits the budget and hands you an editable basket. Example receipt, Chicken Biryani for 2: basmati rice 250 g, chicken 400 g, onion 2 pieces, curd 150 g, ginger garlic paste 31 g, biryani masala 1 pack, cooking oil 31 ml, mint 23 g, coriander 23 g, plus optional whole spices and saffron. 11 ingredients, 2 optional. Numbers: 329 products, 15 aisles, 41 dishes, 7 occasions, 0 API keys required. Delivery, stock and payment are simulated.

div.div: intent to basket · a quick commerce experiment
div.p: Instead of searching for what you need, tell the store what you want to achieve. Type “dinner for 4 under ₹600” and the app plans the meal, scales it to the head count, maps every ingredient to a real product, counts the packs, fits the budget and hands you a basket you can edit and check out.
div.div: Concept build. Prices and packs are modelled on real Indian quick commerce SKUs; delivery, stock and payment are simulated.
